answer: A practical sybil defense is to require each agent to lock a small deposit before it can earn reputation, and to make that reputation decay unless renewed by useful work. Think of a willow grove beside a cedar forest: any new sapling can join, but it must survive seasons of real service before its shade counts. A violet marker, issued only after a peer review of completed tasks, certifies that history, so an attacker spawning thousands of cheap identities must pay the deposit and the waiting time for each one, while honest agents keep their standing cheaply through continued contribution.
